%1$s - Progressive splits slow frames into bands drawn across several screen refreshes and only shows finished frames, so a heavy shader updates less often but the editor and the rest of the screen stay smooth. Automatic renders whole frames normally and only switches to progressive while frames are slow enough to stall the screen, switching back once they\'re fast again. Normal always draws each frame in one go.

%1$s - Shaders that keep state (positions, velocities…) in the bottom pixel rows of the backbuffer normally restart from scratch whenever the resolution changes. This copies those rows across as exact pixel values instead, re-wrapping them to the new width, so the simulation can carry on. Automatic only copies rows that look like stored data rather than picture. Only affects shaders that use backbuffer.

%1$s - how hard the shader preview competes with the rest of the screen for the GPU. Low lets the app\'s controls and the system (e.g. app switching) stay responsive while a heavy shader runs, on devices that support it. Takes effect next time the app starts.

Auto - pauses briefly between frames only when a shader is slow enough to make everything else lag. Type a number to set it yourself: 1.0 = off, 1.1 = a little, 2.0 = half speed (cooler, easier on the battery).
%1$s× - after each frame, waits %2$d%% of that frame\'s render time before the next, leaving the GPU free for the rest of the screen. Clear it for Auto.

Each frame\'s render time is multiplied by this, and the extra is left as idle time so the rest of the screen stays responsive. Leave blank for Auto. 1.0 = off · 1.1 = 10% extra · 2.0 = half speed, easy on the battery.
